ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $ \triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle with a side length of 6. $CE$ bisects the exterior angle $\angle ACF$. Point $D$ is on $AC$, line $BD$ is extended to intersect $CE$ at point $E$. If $CD= \frac{1}{2} AD$, then what is the value of $ \frac{CE}{BC}$? What is the value of $BE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $ \triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle with a side length of 6,\\
$ \therefore AB=BC=6$, $\angle A=\angle ACB=60^\circ$,\\
since $CE$ bisects the exterior angle $\angle ACF$,\\
$ \therefore \angle FCE=\angle DCE=\frac{1}{2}\angle ACF=\frac{1}{2}(180^\circ-\angle ACB)=60^\circ$,\\
in $\triangle ABD$ and $\triangle CED$, $\left\{\begin{array}{l}\angle ADB=\angle CDE \\ \angle A=\angle DCE=60^\circ \end{array}\right.$,\\
$ \therefore \triangle ABD\sim \triangle CED$,\\
$ \therefore \frac{CE}{AB}=\frac{CD}{AD}=\frac{1}{2}$, that is $\frac{CE}{6}=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
solving this gives $CE=3$,\\
$ \therefore \frac{CE}{BC}=\frac{3}{6}=\boxed{\frac{1}{2}}$,\\
as shown, draw $EG\perp BF$ at point $G$,\\
in $Rt\triangle CEG$, $\angle CEG=90^\circ-\angle FCE=30^\circ$,\\
$ \therefore CG=\frac{1}{2}CE=\frac{3}{2}$, $EG=\sqrt{CE^2-CG^2}=\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{3}$,\\
$ \therefore BG=BC+CG=\frac{15}{2}$,\\
in $Rt\triangle BEG$, $BE=\sqrt{BG^2+EG^2}=\sqrt{\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{3}\right)^2}=\boxed{3\sqrt{7}}$.

In triangle ABD and triangle CED, angle ADB and angle CDE are vertical angles, and angle A = angle DCE = 60°, so triangle ABD and triangle CED are similar. Because CE and CF form 60°, CG = CE cos 60° = 3/2, EG = CE sin 60° = 3√3/2. Also BC = 6, so BG = BC + CG = 6 + 3/2 = 15/2. In right triangle BEG, BE = sqrt(BG^2 + EG^2) = sqrt((15/2)^2 + (3√3/2)^2) = sqrt(63) = 3√7.
